tasks.description: Develop the backend logic to calculate and update leaderboard rankings.

tasks.description: Create the frontend interface for displaying hints and tutorials for problems.

tasks.description: Develop the backend to manage hints and tutorials content.

tasks.description: Perform testing to ensure the problem library works as expected.

tasks.name: Test Code Submission and Evaluation
tasks.description: Perform testing to ensure code submission and evaluation works correctly.

tasks.name: Test User Profiles
tasks.description: Perform testing to ensure user profiles are displayed and updated correctly.

tasks.name: Test Leaderboard Functionality
tasks.description: Perform testing to ensure the leaderboard displays accurate rankings.

tasks.name: Test Hints and Tutorials
tasks.description: Perform testing to ensure hints and tutorials are displayed correctly.

tasks.name: Deploy Problem-Solving Platform
tasks.description: Deploy the platform to a production environment.

T1.implementation_approach: Use a design tool like Figma or Adobe XD to create wireframes and prototypes for the Problem Library UI. Focus on user-friendly navigation and search functionality.
T1.notes: Ensure the UI is responsive and accessible.

T2.implementation_approach: Develop RESTful APIs to handle problem creation, retrieval, updating, and deletion. Use MVC architecture for backend implementation.
T2.notes: Ensure proper validation and error handling.

T3.implementation_approach: Design a relational database schema to store problem details, including title, description, difficulty, tags, and test cases.
T3.notes: Optimize schema for search and retrieval.

T4.implementation_approach: Design a user-friendly interface for code submission with syntax highlighting and error feedback.
T4.notes: Include features like code formatting and language selection.

T5.implementation_approach: Implement a sandboxed environment to execute user-submitted code securely and evaluate against test cases.
T5.notes: Ensure security and prevent malicious code execution.

T6.implementation_approach: Create a visually appealing and intuitive user profile page to display user details, achievements, and activity.

T7.implementation_approach: Develop APIs to manage user profile data, including retrieval, updates, and activity logs.
T7.notes: Ensure secure handling of user data.

T8.implementation_approach: Design a leaderboard interface to display user rankings, scores, and achievements.

T9.implementation_approach: Implement backend logic to calculate and update leaderboard rankings based on user performance data.

T10.implementation_approach: Design an interface to display hints and tutorials for problems, with collapsible sections and multimedia support.
T10.notes: Ensure content is easy to navigate and visually appealing.

T11.implementation_approach: Develop APIs to manage hints and tutorials, including creation, retrieval, and updates.

T12.implementation_approach: Write unit and integration tests to verify the functionality of the Problem Library, including API endpoints and UI components.

T13.implementation_approach: Test the code submission and evaluation system by submitting various code snippets and verifying results.
T13.notes: Include edge cases and stress testing.

T14.implementation_approach: Test user profile functionality, including data retrieval, updates, and activity tracking.

T15.implementation_approach: Verify leaderboard functionality by testing ranking calculations and real-time updates.
T15.notes: Test with large datasets for performance.

T16.implementation_approach: Test the hints and tutorials system by verifying content retrieval, updates, and multimedia support.

T17.implementation_approach: Deploy the platform using a cloud service provider. Set up CI/CD pipelines for automated deployment and monitoring.
T17.notes: Ensure scalability and monitor performance post-deployment.

from flask_sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemy

# Initialize the SQLAlchemy object for database operations
db = SQLAlchemy()

from app.database import db

class Problem(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'problems'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True, autoincrement=True)
    title = db.Column(db.String(255), nullable=False, unique=True)
    description = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    difficulty = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=False, server_default=db.func.now())
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=False, server_default=db.func.now(), onupdate=db.func.now())

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<Problem(id={self.id}, title={self.title}, difficulty={self.difficulty})>"

from app.database import db

class User(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'users'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    username = db.Column(db.String(80), unique=True, nullable=False)
    email = db.Column(db.String(120), unique=True, nullable=False)
    password_hash = db.Column(db.String(128), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.current_timestamp())
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.current_timestamp(), onupdate=db.func.current_timestamp())

    def __repr__(self):
        return f'<User {self.username}>'

from app.database import db

class Solution(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'solutions'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    user_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('users.id'), nullable=False)
    problem_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('problems.id'), nullable=False)
    code = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    language = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)
    status = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)  # e.g., 'Accepted', 'Wrong Answer', etc.
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.now())
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.now(), onupdate=db.func.now())

    user = db.relationship('User', backref=db.backref('solutions', lazy=True))
    problem = db.relationship('Problem', backref=db.backref('solutions', lazy=True))

from app.controllers.problem_controller import problem_blueprint
from app.controllers.user_controller import user_blueprint
from app.controllers.solution_controller import solution_blueprint


def register_blueprints(app):
    """
    Register all blueprints to the Flask application.

    :param app: Flask application instance
    """
    app.register_blueprint(problem_blueprint, url_prefix='/problems')
    app.register_blueprint(user_blueprint, url_prefix='/users')
    app.register_blueprint(solution_blueprint, url_prefix='/solutions')

from flask import Flask
from app.database import db
from app.routes import register_blueprints

def create_app():
    # Create Flask app instance
    app = Flask(__name__)

    # Configure the app (add configuration here if needed)
    app.config['SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI'] = 'sqlite:///app.db'
    app.config['SQLALCHEMY_TRACK_MODIFICATIONS'] = False

    # Initialize database
    db.init_app(app)

    # Register blueprints
    register_blueprints(app)

    return app

from app import create_app

app = create_app()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.run()

# ACM Problem-Solving Platform

A website designed to help users solve ACM-style competitive programming problems.

## Features

- Problem Library: A comprehensive library of ACM-style problems categorized by difficulty and topic.
- Code Submission and Evaluation: Allows users to submit code solutions and receive instant feedback on correctness and performance.
- User Profiles: Enables users to create profiles to track their progress, solved problems, and rankings.
- Leaderboard: Displays rankings of users based on their problem-solving performance.
- Hints and Tutorials: Provides hints and tutorials for selected problems to help users improve their skills.

## Setup

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
python app.py
```

## Usage

Open http://localhost:5000 in your browser.
